extracted.intended_audience: undergraduate mathematics students, Putnam contestants, problem solvers and coaches
extracted.subtask_description: The 66th William Lowell Putnam Mathematical Competition problem set (A1–A6, B1–B6). Each item is a contest problem stating what must be proved, constructed, or evaluated; the target work is a correct solution satisfying the stated conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: A1
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that every positive integer is a sum of one or more numbers of the form 2^r 3^s, where r and s are nonnegative integers and no summand divides another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example provided: 23 = 9 + 8 + 6. Requirement: representation as sum of terms of the form 2^r 3^s, with the extra constraint that among the summands no term divides another (i.e., the multiset of summands must be pairwise non-dividing).

rubrics_metrics.name: A2
rubrics_metrics.description: Let S = {(a,b) | a = 1,2,...,n, b = 1,2,3}. A rook tour of S is a polygonal path made up of line segments connecting points p1, p2, ..., p_{3n} in sequence such that (i) p_i ∈ S, (ii) p_i and p_{i+1} are a unit distance apart for 1 ≤ i < 3n, (iii) for each p ∈ S there is a unique i such that p_i = p. How many rook tours are there that begin at (1,1) and end at (n,1)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition of rook tour includes the three conditions listed (membership, unit step adjacency, and visiting each point exactly once). The problem asks for a count of such Hamiltonian lattice paths with given start and end. (An example for n=5 was depicted in original.)

rubrics_metrics.name: A3
rubrics_metrics.description: Let p(z) be a polynomial of degree n all of whose zeros have absolute value 1 in the complex plane. Put g(z) = p(z)/z^{n/2}. Show that all zeros of g'(z) = 0 have absolute value 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data: p has degree n and every root lies on the unit circle. Define g by dividing by z^{n/2} (principal branch implicitly). Requirement: prove that every critical point (zero of the derivative) of g also lies on the unit circle (has modulus 1).

rubrics_metrics.name: A4
rubrics_metrics.description: Let H be an n × n matrix all of whose entries are ±1 and whose rows are mutually orthogonal. Suppose H has an a × b submatrix whose entries are all 1. Show that ab ≤ n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hypotheses: H is a Hadamard-like matrix with ±1 entries and orthogonal rows. There is a contiguous (or unspecified location) submatrix of size a by b consisting entirely of 1's. Goal: deduce the inequality ab ≤ n.

rubrics_metrics.name: A5
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute this definite integral exactly; no extra conditions. (Integral bounds and integrand as stated.)

rubrics_metrics.name: A6
rubrics_metrics.description: Let n be given, n ≥ 4, and suppose that P1, P2, ..., Pn are n randomly, independently and uniformly chosen points on a circle. Consider the convex n-gon whose vertices are the P_i. What is the probability that at least one of the vertex angles of this polygon is acute?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Random model: points chosen independently and uniformly on the circumference; polygon formed by those points in convex position (take convex hull). Compute probability that the polygon has at least one acute internal angle.

rubrics_metrics.name: B1
rubrics_metrics.description: Find a nonzero polynomial P(x,y) such that P(a,2a) = 0 for all real numbers a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirement: construct (or exhibit) a nonzero two-variable polynomial P with real coefficients that vanishes on the entire line {(a,2a): a ∈ ℝ} in the plane, i.e., P(x,y) has the line y=2x as a subset of its zero set.

rubrics_metrics.name: B2
rubrics_metrics.description: Find all positive integers n, k_1, ..., k_n such that k_1 + ··· + k_n = 5n − 4 and 1/k_1 + ··· + 1/k_n = 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Find all integer solutions (n and the positive integers k_i) satisfying both the sum and reciprocal-sum constraints simultaneously.

rubrics_metrics.name: B3
rubrics_metrics.description: Find all differentiable functions f : (0, ∞) → (0, ∞) for which there is a positive real number a such that f'(a/x) = x / f(x) for all x > 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unknowns: differentiable positive-valued functions on (0,∞) and a positive parameter a. Functional-differential relation links derivative at a/x to reciprocal of f(x) times x. Determine all such f (and corresponding a).

rubrics_metrics.name: B4
rubrics_metrics.description: For positive integers m and n, let f(m,n) denote the number of n-tuples (x_1, x_2, ..., x_n) of integers such that |x_1| + |x_2| + ··· + |x_n| ≤ m. Show that f(m,n) = f(n,m).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combinatorial equality: the number of integer lattice points in the ℓ1-ball of radius m in ℤ^n equals the number in the ℓ1-ball of radius n in ℤ^m. Prove a bijection or counting argument establishing symmetry in m and n.

rubrics_metrics.name: B5
rubrics_metrics.description: Let P(x_1, ..., x_n) denote a polynomial with real coefficients in the variables x_1, ..., x_n, and suppose that (∂^2/∂x_1^2 + ··· + ∂^2/∂x_n^2) P = 0 (identically) and that (1 + x_1^2 + ··· + x_n^2) divides P(x_1, ..., x_n). Show that P = 0 identically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation: P is a (real-coefficient) polynomial which is harmonic (Laplacian zero) and is divisible by the polynomial 1 + x_1^2 + ... + x_n^2. Conclude that the only possibility is the zero polynomial.

rubrics_metrics.name: B6
rubrics_metrics.description: Let S_n denote the set of all permutations of the numbers 1,2,...,n. For π ∈ S_n, let σ(π) = 1 if π is even and σ(π) = −1 if π is odd. Also, let ν(π) denote the number of fixed points of π. Show that ∑_{π∈S_n} σ(π)/(ν(π)+1) = (−1)^{n+1} n/(n+1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sum over all permutations of the signed reciprocal of (number of fixed points + 1). Goal: evaluate closed-form sum giving (−1)^{n+1} n/(n+1).
